- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if price has already broken below 10-day moving average.  
- After a spike in price (forecast > 70.5), reduce forecast by 2–3 points in next 3 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and forecast deviates > 2.5% from recent 7-day average, apply mean reversion correction toward the 7-day mean.  
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling (e.g., 0.6–1.0 with downward trend), reduce forecast slope by 15–20% to avoid false momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 1–2 points below forecast, reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.0 point to align with recent underperformance.  
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is below 68.0, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0 point to reflect bullish sentiment bias.  
- Avoid forecasting below 65.0 unless sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4) and price has broken below 60-day moving average.
